the sacroiliitis in children and adolescents is difficult to diagnose.

the SIJ in children and adolescents is very dynamic, and the anatomy is constantly changing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in children, the sacrum has three separate vertebral bodies and the SIJ has three distinct joints.
ossification of the nuclei is a normal finding that can persist into adolescence, but should be differentiated from sacroiliitis.
